items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: They had Herbie Ellis and Ray Brown, myself, that was the rhythm, and Jack Sheldon, put on Pete Candoli and Bill Berry.

ctx.x: Who was in the pit, in the show band?

In New York we had Billy Watrous, Danny Stiles and Bill Berry. Then we added like Ziggy Harrell and Roy Eldridge, and on sax we had Roger Pemberton, tenor, Shelly Gould, and Richie Kamuka. Then Richie had to figure out whether to add Zoot Sims or Al Cohn, then Jim Hall was the guitar, and he took off and we got Jim Raney or somebody like that. And Jimmy refused to play any of this rock & roll stuff for Sonny. He refused to do it. So they brought in another guy. So now we had two guitars. Chuck Wayne and Jim Hall.…

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I have it with Jake Hanna, the drummer.

ctx.x: Can you tell us other musicians that you’ve had that chemistry with?

Oh let me see. Well there’s a lot of them. I had it with Sweets Edison, he’s here at the festival, you know. And I have it with Jake Hanna, the drummer. And of course I have it with Ray Brown to a great extent. We love to play together. So there could be more but I can’t name them all.
Could you also explain to guitarists how that it takes an impeccable sense of time to play in a trio with no drums.
